Feiten (Y20)

Region in the English rating survey: Haless.

In one sentence: Begin with a battered trading league on the Jellyfish Coast and use whale oil, ports and artificer research to turn paper lanterns into airships travelling around Halann.

Story: high | Mission-tree length: very long (80 definitions, including unfinished Insyaa nodes) | Mission-tree currency: local file modified on 2026-09-07, supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: very high | Grind: medium-high (early neighbours and later infrastructure/technology gates) | Early pressure: high | Expansion capacity: high, prioritising trade networks and overseas outposts

From a refuge coast to a merchant league

Feiten is the native English name of Y20, rendered as 飞腾 in the current Chinese localisation. It is already a selectable coastal republic in 1444, not a Tag awaiting formation. Existing province-history research establishes seven provinces under Y20, while country history sets the League of Feiten reform, Gangim culture, High Philosophy and the Silk Turban school. The starting ruler is Zongmin Kai, installed in 1440 and given the Entrepreneur trait. Luoyip is a historical friend, alongside local historical rivals. The current Mod determines these opening institutions and territories.

The offline English League of Feiten page mainly lists the coast, capital, government and ruler, with little historical narrative. The original Chinese offline Wiki adds an earlier origin: as Jaher's legions advanced along the Yanhe, refugees fled south to the Jellyfish Coast, where they and their descendants formed a league amid the disorder following the expulsion of the Sun Elves. That page gives no exact foundation year. This is worldbuilding context, not grounds for inventing a dated battle or treating the mission tree's trading empire as an accomplished fact in 1444. The historical-map research currently anchors Y20's seven starting provinces in 1444 but is still assembling subsequent dates; it cannot establish a settled chronology of Feiten's expansion. The current English Mod primer independently contains the refugee-to-league account; that corroboration does not supply a precise foundation date.

Feiten's present wealth is not secure. Dedicated mission text says pirate queen Ping Shuang's rebellion stole part of the fleet and burned the harbour district. War with Zyujyut gained Cuihiok, the gateway to the tea forests, but left inhabitants to pacify and forests not yet controlled. The opening campaign is therefore not immediate airship domination: rebuild shipyards, protect two harbours, handle piracy and tea commerce, then compete with large river cities such as Tianlou.

How whale-oil lanterns become airships

Feiten's distinctive development begins in local life. The Jellyfish Festival traditionally releases paper lanterns lit with whale oil. State-organised whaling makes oil, whalebone and experimental materials more available, prompting a question: could silk envelopes, controlled flames and a basket turn lanterns into vessels carrying people? Missions and events develop this idea through Shuimu balloons, reconnaissance, engineers, artificer inventions, steam power and skyports, rather than supplying a mature air force at the start. Whaling events can even send the ruler to sea, risking injury and returning with different catches.

The House of Fire and Water, exchanges with gnomes, aerial tactics, coal and optics later connect economic construction tightly to invention. A skyport is not simply a permanent modifier: an event menu lets the player establish Skyposts in eligible trade-node provinces, while missions require effective air facilities, engineering workshops and inventions in sufficient numbers. The eventual first airship flight can unlock commercial and military skyship inventions, and the sky-lord endpoint requires substantial national power and an established global network. These are campaign goals in current scripts, not Feiten's starting technological level. Its national ideas likewise emphasise commerce, naval power, mobility and range rather than land conquest alone.

More than peaceful commerce

Feiten earns money through sea routes, salt roads and tea plantations, but also uses diplomacy, espionage and warfare to capture markets. Luoyip can become a western partner; Tianlou is the sharpest commercial rival. The Tianlou mission accommodates different circumstances: controlling the city can lead to a trade-agreement event, whereas a siege or assault route triggers bombing. The latter causes actual devastation and development losses in local scripts and can damage temple facilities. A sky-trading republic is not automatically a gentle liberal state, nor must every player's route bomb Tianlou.

Maritime missions lead towards whaling bases, island supply stations, oceanic trade and Aelantir. Trade contacts extend to Rahen, Sarhal and other regions before turning to worldwide routes. However, connected nodes for breaking through the Storm Gates and entering Insyaa's interior still contain TODO once Insyaa is in in the current script. Official development discussions of Insyaa expansion in 2026 do not prove that these particular nodes are now functional locally. The file contains 80 definitions unlocked in stages, not 80 missions all supplied with complete triggers and effects. Feiten's main campaign continues as Y20; no mandatory successor-state finale has been established.

Personality and recommendations

The v2.1 coordinates are expansion 78/100 | autocracy 45/100 | magic–artifice direction 12/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 96/100) | pluralism 66/100. Its phase profile moves from damaged merchant league and port reconstruction (expansion 58, theme intensity 25) to airships, skyports and global trade (expansion 85, theme intensity 96).

Its v2.1 values classification is Neutral (55/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory. Port security, industrial development and knowledge exchange support public prosperity. National ideas describe extensive use of pressed convicts as crews; the Tianlou siege route can cause severe devastation and development losses. Controlling Tianlou instead allows a trade-agreement route, so bombing is not inevitable. Trade, colonisation or warfare alone do not determine good or evil; specific coercive means lower dignity and restraint.

Recommended for players who enjoy a paper-lantern-to-airship technological narrative, maritime commerce, global routes and a long, interconnected tree. Players expecting an immediately available air force, disliking stronger early neighbours and complex construction gates, or requiring the Insyaa direction to be fully implemented will be disappointed. Older Reddit accounts often describe a wealthy late game and difficult opening; these are version-bound experiences, not current numerical conclusions. See the original evidence page for references and gaps and the English source-text receipt for this translation's checks.

National ideas (reference appendix)

Native English national-idea names and descriptions are reproduced below with the inherited effect displays. Traditions apply when this set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Alternative sets and successor ideas do not automatically stack. Descriptions may recount history or depict future ideals, not events already completed in 1444. Native English wording is reused rather than back-translating embellished Chinese localisation. Inherited display-unit assumptions remain unverified; this translation does not correct source data.

Feiten (Y20) — Feiten Ideas

Traditions: Feiten Traditions

Effects: Global trade power: +15%; Naval Morale: +10%.

Idea 1: Organized Impressment

Feiten commands a vast fleet, far too large for us to completely crew with our own citizens without crippling other industries. Since the founding of the League in the mid 1300s, we have taken to pressing prisoners and criminals to serve on our vessels, working for their freedom and granting us the manpower at sea we so desperately require, even if such employment sometimes backfires.

Effects: Sailor Modifier: +15%.

Idea 2: Where the Wind Blows

Like our famous balloons, Feiten drifts with the winds of change. We are good to our allies, so long as they benefit us, and cruel to our enemies until it is no longer reasonable to act as such.

Some may call us 'deceitful' or 'untrustworthy', but at the end of the day, it is simply the nature of things - and it helps that we always come out on top.

Effects: Diplomatic relations: +1; Change rival cost: -25%.

Idea 3: Jellyfish Festival

The New Year's celebrations in Feiten are legendary across Yanshen and beyond, as our skies fill with the most elegant and beautifully crafted balloons, the wealthy looking out over the Jellyfish Coast and our city from their gondolas. Meanwhile, the lower classes release clouds of paper lanterns to brighten the night sky. Truly a sight to behold.

Effects: National unrest: -1.5.

Idea 4: Balloon Scouts

Our balloons are not just for festivities and presentations; several smaller crafts accompany our armed forces to scout out their routes with a bird's eye view, greatly increasing the ability of our armies to plan their passage through rough terrain.

Effects: Movement speed: +15%.

Idea 5: Whale Lanterns

The whaling industry is key to our civilization - whale oil not only burns in the furnaces that take our balloons to the sky, but also brightens our city streets. Instead of using cloth or charcoal torches, glass lanterns hang from streetside poles and burn throughout the evenings, astonishing visitors with their longevity and brilliance.

Effects: Prestige decay: -1%.

Idea 6: Diokzatgun

The revolt of Ping Shuang and her theft of our fleet taught us an important lesson about piracy and the risks of using press-ganged crews. Nowadays, an entire quarter of the Feiten fleet is made up of Diokzatgun, pirate hunters crewed only with citizens of Feiten, trained extensively in naval combat, and granted impunity in assaulting vessels they have reason to believe may have fallen to brigands and mutiny.

Effects: Heavy ship combat ability: +10%.

Idea 7: To The Ends Of Halann

Our vessels, either on the sea or in the air, are common sights across the world. In every coastal marketplace from Anbenncóst to Ynnsmouth, and even south towards Ormam, our traders carry the seal of our city, projecting our mercantile power a world over.

Effects: Trade range: +25%.

Ambition: Feiten Ambition

Effects: Ship trade power: +15%.
